reasons: Only the setup and fact builder were provided, so the test cases could not be checked.
Three sections of this file were not included in the packet.

terms.meaning: A single project statement with its source, field and assessment.
A fact that has passed the source and meaning checks, so it can be used.

sections.name: File setup, admittedAssessment
sections.title: Test setup and standard passing assessment
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the spreadsheet library, the collection and scan helpers, and defines a standard passing assessment record that the tests reuse.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests need a stand-in assessment that looks admitted so they can focus on the step being tested.
sections.watch_out: The shared assessment is made up, so passing tests show the logic works, not that real sources are good.

sections.name: fact
sections.title: Builds a test fact
sections.what: Creates a made-up project fact with an identifier, field, text, source link and assessment. A flag decides whether it counts as admitted or only as partial.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests need both admitted and unadmitted facts to confirm that only admitted ones are used.
sections.watch_out: Source links point to a reserved invalid domain, so they cannot be followed and exist only for tests.

sections.name: ledger, capture, extracted (part 1)
sections.title: Money, price basis and date tests
sections.what: Builds a fake project record for the tests, then checks that research values are used only when admitted and unconflicted, that money amounts and currencies are read correctly, that price basis differences are flagged, and that partial dates such as Q3 2024 convert correctly.
sections.why: Likely reason: fixed example inputs make it clear when a change breaks money or date reading.
sections.watch_out: The fake record is cast to a type, so it can drift from the real record shape without an error.

sections.name: ledger, capture, extracted (part 2)
sections.title: Overrun, reason, FX and page date tests
sections.what: Checks that overrun percentages and delay months are read from wording, that overrun reasons come only from admitted passages, that the value chain lookup and gap query limit behave, that the World Bank exchange rate keeps its source, and that publication dates are read from page markup. It also sets up a fake source capture for the later tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: each rule is pinned with a small example so later edits to the helpers are checked.
sections.watch_out: The World Bank test uses a fake fetch, so a change in the real service would not be caught here.

sections.name: register
sections.title: Source policy and spreadsheet export tests
sections.what: Defines a helper that gives each source an identifier, then tests that banned or undated sources are skipped before capture, and that the spreadsheet export writes every tab with the right calculation and reason rows.
sections.why: Likely reason: these rules decide what enters the evidence, so they receive direct checks.
sections.watch_out: The source policy test uses made-up host names, so it proves the rule works but not the real site lists.

summary: Test file for the scan inputs step; only its setup and fact builder were provided, so most of its checks could not be reviewed.
purpose: Checks that the scan inputs step handles facts, currencies, dates, workbooks and sources correctly.
why: Likely reason: the scan inputs step decides what evidence goes into later steps, so it has its own tests.
how: Creates made-up facts and assessments, then runs the inputs step on them and checks the results.
inputs: Made-up facts and assessments defined in the file, and the functions imported from the scan inputs and collection code.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test.
risks: Only two of the five sections were available, so the rules tested in the remaining sections are unknown here.
debug: Read the failing assertion, then open the matching function in scanInputs.ts. Re-read the full file before relying on any claim about what it tests.
